A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same adaptive-kernel study. Their main text, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original neural-network simulations and numerical kernel calculations, including losses, kernel alignments, and activation distributions on CIFAR10, MNIST, and synthetic data.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds tanh-network kernel comparisons and activation-distribution analyses.

M1.justification: The aNBK min-max solver and aNTK dynamical mean-field procedure remain the proposed methods. Lazy initialization and layer-dependent priors already appear in v1; the tanh experiments exercise the existing general Bayesian formulation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR10, binary MNIST, and synthetic whitened inputs. MNIST digits 0/1 already appear in v1 Figure 6. The added tanh experiments change model configurations within existing coverage; the animate/inanimate description clarifies the retained CNN experiment.

E2.justification: The lazy NNGP/NNGPK, initial-kernel, and finite-width network comparisons are retained. v2 associates the existing finite-width curves with Pacelli et al. (2023), but Figure 9 reproduces v1 Figure 7 rather than adding a comparator.

E3.justification: New Figure 4 evaluates deep tanh networks on P=50 MNIST examples, initializes the theoretical solver from lazy kernels, and reports theory-versus-empirical kernel alignment. The earlier P=1000 ReLU/CIFAR10 experiment remains as Figure 7. Most additional settings in Appendix G are newly disclosed details.

E4.justification: v2 adds a deep-network solver check using lazy initialization and a tanh analysis of kernel adaptation and preactivation densities across feature-learning strengths. These supplement the retained depth, finite-width, and fixed-point analyses; the original warm-start experiment is preserved.

E5.justification: Appendix G.4 newly documents Langevin averaging every 1,000 steps after step 5,000 within 20,000-step runs. This adds statistical-estimation information without establishing additional independent runs. No new confidence intervals, significance tests, or independent-seed replication counts are reported.

E6.justification: New Figure 4 reports theory–empirical kernel alignments of 97%, 81%, 73%, and 89% across four displayed layers. Figure 6 adds tanh kernel results and a bimodal preactivation-density finding. Existing principal loss curves and the relocated ReLU results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 corrects coefficients and scaling in Bayesian saddle-point and DMFT equations and adds formal comparisons with earlier scaling theories in Appendix B. The main theoretical results remain. The added regression derivation contains an inconsistency: Equation (40) omits the β/λ prefactor implied by Equations (28) and (39).

C1.justification: The abstract, six main contributions, and discussion retain their central claims. Section 1.1 adds an explicit first-to-solve novelty claim for Bayesian adaptive kernels without richness perturbation or Gaussian approximations, sharpening the claimed distinction from prior work.

C2.justification: v2 explains discrepancies in the new deep-network comparison through difficulties solving coupled non-Gaussian min-max problems. Appendix G.6 adds a substantive computational limitation: the theoretical solvers can be substantially more expensive than finite-width network training, extending v1's brief call for cheaper solvers.

D1.justification: The brief implementation appendix becomes a detailed account of preprocessing, both solvers, MLP/CNN training, and computational costs. Newly documented information includes image resizing, Monte Carlo sample counts, optimization budgets, update sizes, learning rates, temperature, regularization, and JAX/Optax/Flax implementation choices.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 and new Appendix B substantially expand positioning against scale-renormalization theories, adaptive kernels under NTK scaling, and likelihood-rescaling approaches. Six references are added, including Fischer et al. (2024). v1's broad characterization of earlier predictors is replaced with more differentiated comparisons.

P1.justification: The exposition is substantially expanded and reorganized: related work gains a three-part appendix, implementation guidance becomes six structured subsections, and the original deep-MLP discussion moves to the appendix while the main text presents the tanh example. The central methodological narrative remains largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 4 and 6, relocates and rearranges v1 Figure 4 as Figure 7, and corrects Figure 1's panel descriptions and axis terminology. Algorithm formatting and captions are revised, while most existing graphics and Table 1 retain their displays.

improvement.justification: The added lazy-initialized solver validation, detailed numerical documentation, and clearer distinctions from prior work improve assessability and reproducibility. These gains are tempered by inconsistencies in the new material, notably Equation (40)'s missing β/λ prefactor. The net improvement is useful but falls short of a comprehensive strengthening of the paper's reliability.
